subject: English
text: What is the name of the girl who couldn't hear but became a famous percussionist?
explanation: Evelyn Glennie is a multi-percussionist who achieved international success despite having a profound hearing impairment.

options.text: Kezia
Evelyn Glennie
Margie
Santosh Yadav

subject: English
text: In 'The Little Girl', how did Kezia's grandmother help Kezia when she had a nightmare?
explanation: It was actually her father who carried her to his big bedroom and slept next to her, while her grandmother was not in the room.

options.text: Her grandmother sang a lullaby
Her father carried her to his room and slept next to her
Her mother gave her medicine
Her cook Olga read her a story

subject: English
text: In 'A Truly Beautiful Mind', what did Albert Einstein's headmaster tell his father about him?
explanation: The headmaster told Einstein's father that Einstein would never make a success at anything, no matter what profession he chose.

options.text: That he was a genius who would win a Nobel Prize
That he would never make a success at anything
That he should become a professional musician
That he was too smart for the school

explanation: The child ran after dragonflies and butterflies to catch them in his hands.

options.text: A small rabbit
Dragonflies and butterflies
A toy carriage
His father's shadow

subject: English
text: In the poem 'Wind', who are the 'weaklings' the wind makes fun of?
explanation: The wind makes fun of weak things like crumbling houses, crumbling doors, and weak bodies.

options.text: The birds flying in the sky
Crumbling houses, doors, rafters, and weak bodies
The rich merchants of the town
The small children playing outside

subject: English

explanation: A great red ruby was glowing on the hilt of his sword, which he gave to the poor seamstress.

options.text: Sapphire
Ruby
Diamond
Emerald

subject: English
text: In 'A Truly Beautiful Mind', why did Albert Einstein migrate to the USA in 1933?
explanation: Einstein emigrated to the United States in 1933 because the Nazis had come to power in Germany.

options.text: To accept a research fellowship at Oxford
Because the Nazis had come to power in Germany
To build the atomic bomb with American scientists
To work as a consultant for the US patent office

subject: English
text: Choose the correct reported speech form: 'He said, "I may go out tonight."'
explanation: 'May' changes to 'might', 'tonight' changes to 'that night', and the tense of the reporting verb requires backshifting.

options.text: He said that he may go out that night.
He said that he might go out that night.
He told that he might go out tonight.
He said that I might go out that night.

subject: English
text: In 'The Sound of Music' (Part I), how does Evelyn Glennie hear music?
explanation: She hears it not through her ears, but by sensing the notes and vibrations through different parts of her body.

options.text: By using a special hearing aid developed in London
By sensing the vibrations through different parts of her body
By reading sheet music and lip-reading teachers
By playing only wind instruments

subject: English
text: Fill in the blank with the correct determiners: 'There is ___ water in the jug; you can drink it.'
explanation: 'A little' has a positive meaning (some, though not much), which matches the statement 'you can drink it'.

options.text: little
a little
few
a few

subject: English
text: In the poem 'The Road Not Taken', why does the poet choose the second road?
explanation: Because it was grassy, wanted wear, and looked less traveled by people.

options.text: Because it was clean and concrete
Because it was grassy and wanted wear
Because it had signboards pointing to the town
Because his friends had taken that path

subject: English
text: In 'In the Kingdom of Fools', who was arrested first for the wall collapse that killed the thief?
explanation: The merchant, who owned the house whose wall collapsed, was summoned first.

options.text: The bricklayer who built the wall
The merchant who owned the house
The dancing girl who distracted the bricklayer
The goldsmith who delayed the dancing girl's work

subject: English
text: In 'The Beggar', how did Lushkoff become a notary earning thirty-five roubles a month?

options.text: He bought a commercial shop using advocate's money
Sergei recommended him to a friend for copying work, which led to a notary job
He won a litigation with Sergei's help
He was hired by a choir group again

subject: English
text: Choose the sentence that displays correct verb agreement for plural-appearing singular nouns: 'The news ___ not good today.'
explanation: 'News' is an uncountable singular noun, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

options.text: are
is
were
have been

subject: English
text: In 'The Last Leaf', what did Sue tell Johnsy about Behrman's death at the end of the story?
explanation: She told Johnsy that Behrman died of pneumonia after painting the last leaf on the wall in the freezing rain.

options.text: That he was admitted to a hospital in Boston
That he died of pneumonia after painting the last leaf to save her life
That he retired to a village in Germany
That he died of old age in his bed

subject: English
text: In 'The Happy Prince', where did the Prince's sapphire eyes go?

options.text: Both were given to the poor seamstress for her sick son
One to a playwright in a garret, and the other to a poor matchgirl
Both were sold to buy food for the swallow
They were stolen by the Town Councillors

subject: English
text: Identify the grammatically correct passive voice of: 'Who wrote this letter?'
explanation: 'Who' becomes 'By whom', and the simple past active 'wrote' changes to 'was written'.

options.text: By whom this letter was written?
By whom was this letter written?
Who was this letter written by?
By whom had this letter been written?

subject: English
text: In the poem 'Wind', how can we make the wind our friend according to the poet?
explanation: By building strong houses, closing doors firmly, and making ourselves physically and mentally strong.

options.text: By burning fires to stop the cold breeze
By building strong homes, joining doors firmly, and making ourselves strong
By praying to the wind god everyday
By planting dense trees around our houses

subject: English
text: In 'A House Is Not a Home', why did the author hate visiting his old school after his house burned down?
explanation: He felt embarrassed and awkward in his old clothes and shoes, feeling like a homeless person with no belongings.

options.text: Because the teachers there were very strict
Because he felt embarrassed and awkward in his borrowed clothes and shoes
Because the school building had also caught fire
Because he had not completed his homework

subject: English
text: Complete the sentence with the correct tense of the verb: 'If you had run faster, you ___ the race.'
explanation: This is a third conditional sentence; the main clause must use 'would have + past participle'.

options.text: would win
would have won
had won
will have won

subject: English
text: In 'The Sound of Music' (Part II), who modified the pungi into the modern shehnai?

A barber of a family of professional musicians
A court poet of Aurangzeb
A French music exporter

subject: English
text: In the poem 'The Road Not Taken', what is the significance of the sigh in the final stanza?
explanation: The sigh represents the poet's reflective, slightly regretful realization that he can never know what the other road held, highlighting the gravity of irreversible choices.

options.text: It shows his physical exhaustion after walking a long distance
It represents reflective contemplation of the irreversible nature of life's choices
It indicates his anger at having chosen the wrong path
It highlights his joy of discovering a treasure on the road

subject: English
text: In 'The Last Leaf', what did Johnsy's dependency on the falling leaves represent psychologically?
explanation: It represented her loss of hope and a self-destructive belief that her life was fading away, linking her survival to external, transient objects.

options.text: Her passion for studying botany and nature
Her psychological loss of hope and externalized sense of control over her own life
Her fear of seasonal changes in New York
Her artistic desire to paint autumn landscapes

subject: English
text: Identify the type of clause underlined in the sentence: 'The plan <u>which he proposed</u> was rejected by the manager.'
explanation: The underlined clause describes/modifies the noun 'plan', making it an Adjective (or Relative) Clause.

options.text: Noun Clause
Adjective Clause
Adverb Clause of Reason
Noun Clause acting as Object

subject: English
text: Analyze the sentence: 'He behaves as if he ___ the boss of the company.' Which verb form is correct here?
explanation: In hypothetical comparison clauses introduced by 'as if/as though', 'were' is used for all subjects to show unreality.

options.text: is
were
was
would be
